analysis:
Examined all five batch analyses and the supplied source replay. No independently supported security regression qualifies. Replay confirms repeatable work-disk documentation, status decoding and informational capacity rendering: docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1094-1132,1249-1258; SandboxAddon.swift:154-173,211-225; SandboxEligibility.swift:247-262. Status parsing skips malformed entries and clamps negative slot totals; these fields do not establish serving authorization. The changelog at changelog.d/sandbox-setup-work-disks.md:3-8 describes separate ownership consent and refusal on failed disk plans or unsupported installers.

Together, the changes expand VM/job storage onto external volumes and introduce an optional privileged ownership operation, relevant to A-019/TB-013/T-061 and A-018/TB-012/T-059. Local analyses report argv-based forwarding, explicit consent, root refusal and fail-closed planning in SandboxInstaller.swift:107-137 and SandboxSetupCommand.swift:84-88,291-367,435-446,480-485, but those implementations are omitted from this replay and cannot be independently validated here. Test assertions are not proof of production enforcement.

Remaining material review: inspect SandboxWorkDisk.swift path/mount validation and enableOwnership execution, including fixed executable/argument handling and foreground sudo behavior; verify check-to-install volume replacement handling. Confirm the add-on's disk validation, private storage, missing-drive behavior and protection of running paid jobs. These are unverified contracts, not findings of absent controls. Reconcile external VM/job storage and volume-wide ownership changes with TB-013/A-019. T-041 protects a distinct inference-cache subsystem and does not establish sandbox-disk encryption. No replayed change modifies attestation, token custody, hop encryption or billing enforcement. Replay omits 30 of 35 source units, leaving these security conclusions unresolved.
